newsitem.title: USA: Fate of Olympic 'french-fry' cauldron up in air.
newsitem.headline: Fate of Olympic 'french-fry' cauldron up in air.

text.p: The Olympic cauldron lit by Muhammad Ali at the opening of the 1996 Summer Games could be torn down or destroyed due to a lack of sufficent funds for its upkeep, supporters said on Monday.
"If we move it, we're going to lose the history," Douglas Dean, a leader of the Summerhill neighbourhood adjacent to the stadium, said.

The metal structure, which critics have called a giant french fry container, is located next to the Olympic stadium, which is being converted into Turner Field for the Atlanta Braves baseball team. The Braves have not agreed to maintain the cauldron, citing maintenance and insurance costs. Team president Stan Kasten said recently he wanted the cauldron moved.

Several independent efforts have been launched to save the cauldron. An attorney said he would pay for its upkeep if he could post a plaque honouring his immigrant Lebanese grandfather. A woman has reactivated her Keep The Cauldron committee to raise money for its preservation. The artist who designed the cauldron also wants it to stay.
"They could make it a tourist attraction," Dean said. "I think that fans and other visitors to Atlanta will come to the south side of the city to see the cauldron."

Millions of people worldwide watched on television as the 54-year-old Ali, his arm shaking from Parkinson's Syndrome, lit the cauldron's flame at the close of the Games' opening ceremonies on July 19.
